origin: cwe/79/javascript Taint Sinks: Angular [innerHTML] and DomSanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustHtml()

finding.name: Cross-site Scripting
finding.summary: bypassSecurityTrustHtml() tells Angular's DomSanitizer to treat rawBody as already-safe HTML and skip its own sanitization entirely. rawBody is untrusted comment content, so any script-carrying markup in it is rendered unescaped wherever the returned value is bound to [innerHTML].

trap: Keeping bypassSecurityTrustHtml() but pre-filtering rawBody with a denylist (stripping <script> tags, or blocking a few known-dangerous attribute names) before the call does not close this: bypassSecurityTrustHtml() disables Angular's own sanitizer for whatever value it returns, so any vector the hand-rolled filter misses - an onerror handler, a javascript: URL in an href, an <svg onload=...> - reaches [innerHTML] unescaped, and a denylist reliably misses some of these. The fix is to stop calling bypassSecurityTrustHtml() on user-controlled content: either bind rawBody straight to [innerHTML] and let Angular's default DomSanitizer run (it strips dangerous markup automatically), or, if a broader set of formatting tags needs to be allowed than Angular's own sanitizer permits, sanitize with DOMPurify.sanitize() first and bind that result without any bypass call.
must_preserve: Comment bodies still render their allowed formatting (for example <b>, <em>, <a>) in the page. No markup in rawBody can execute script in the viewer's browser, regardless of which tag or attribute it uses.
